requirements.evidence: The task is implemented end to end: the three reversible migrations and models/factories (`database/migrations/2026_10_20_120000_create_totems_table.php`, `2026_10_20_120001_create_totem_presets_table.php`, `2026_10_20_120002_create_totem_preset_queue_table.php`), the command with a cryptographically random zero-padded code, 10-min expiry, consumed reset and audit (`app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:15-47`), code format/expiry/consumption checks and JWT issuance (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemAuthController.php:20-108`), middleware claim/state/entity checks and the queue intersection (`app/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTotem.php:23-60`), entity-scoped queue resolution with 404/403 (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemApiController.php:118-128`), 201 ticket issuance with channel `totem` through `IssueTicket` (`:83-107`), 30/min limiter (`app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:41-42`), CORS (`config/cors.php:7-21`), env/phpunit entries and doc updates.

conventions.evidence: Follows most conventions: generated-style reversible migrations with `down()`, deliberate `#[Fillable]` on both models (`app/Models/Totem.php:13`, `app/Models/TotemPreset.php:10-18`), factories, and reuse of `IssueTicket` instead of a service layer; docs and CHANGELOG are updated. Deviations: the pairing domain write is inline in the controller (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemAuthController.php:26-96`) rather than an `app/Actions/*` class, and `composer.json:13` adds a runtime dependency without a visible `composer.lock` update.

security.evidence: No weakness found. The JWT signature/expiry are verified with firebase/php-jwt (`app/Support/TotemJwt.php:47-68`); the middleware re-checks totem, preset and entity state and recomputes the effective scope server-side (`AuthenticateTotem.php:37-60`); queue lookup is entity-scoped and scope-checked (`TotemApiController.php:118-128`); pairing code format is strict and all pairing failures return the same body (`TotemAuthController.php:20-24,30-57`); the code is hidden from serialization and never logged (`app/Models/TotemPreset.php:30`, `TotemAuthController.php:112-115`); CORS is origin-restricted with credentials disabled (`config/cors.php:13-21`). Input is validated server-side and the priority accepts only the enum values (`TotemApiController.php:131-137`).

tests.evidence: A broad Pest feature suite covers the command (`tests/Feature/Totem/TotemApiTest.php:39-58`), pairing success/consumption (`:63-92`), malformed/missing/expired/consumed/inactive/unknown codes (`:94-125`), regeneration and pairing throttling (`:120-135`), missing/garbage/forged/expired tokens and inactive/mismatched state (`:139-177`), last_seen updates and entity forbidden (`:179-195`), queue order/scope removal (`:199-237`), priorities and 404/403/422 (`:241-276`), ticket issuance/validation/throttle (`:280-340`), and CORS (`:344-373`). Missing: assertions on the audit entries required for pairing success/failure (and that the full code is absent).

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: priorities live in one enum used by both read and write paths (`app/Enums/TicketPriority.php:11-38`), ticket issuance reuses `IssueTicket` (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemApiController.php:97-99`), and there is no service/repository layer. Small duplication: the entity-limited preset queue query appears in both `app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemAuthController.php:67-71` and `app/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTotem.php:48-52`.

readability.evidence: Clear names, typed signatures, small methods and useful PHPDoc (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemApiController.php:22-107`, `app/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTotem.php:23-60`). Minor readability issues: the `$queue` route parameter is reused as a `Queue|JsonResponse` (`TotemApiController.php:60-90`), and the limiter block splits the `layouts` comment from the Blade call it describes (`app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:37-44`).

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task: routes, models, migrations, command, JWT, middleware, CORS, env/phpunit, and the required docs. The queue `appearance` overrides for color/icon/description (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemApiController.php:38-49`) are an extra presentation feature not requested by `task.md`.

issues.explanation: Pairing is a domain write (consume the code, create the Totem, issue the JWT), but it is implemented inline in the HTTP controller; the project routes domain writes through `app/Actions/*` like `IssueTicket`, so this use case has no action boundary.

The diff adds the `firebase/php-jwt` runtime dependency but contains no `composer.lock` update; if the lock is tracked, `composer install` will not provide the `Firebase\JWT\*` classes imported by `app/Support/TotemJwt.php` and the tests, so confirm and commit the lock.

The shared-errors table says 429 can come from any `api/*` route, but only `/api/totem/auth` and the ticket route carry throttle middleware; the queues and priorities GETs never return 429, so the documented contract is broader than the code.

Queue color/icon/description overrides read from `totem_presets.appearance['queues']` are an extra feature not requested by the task; they add branches that the tests do not exercise (only defaults are asserted).

No test asserts the audit entries written on pairing success/failure or by `totem:pairing-code`, nor that the full code is absent, although audit logging is an explicit requirement (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemAuthController.php:82-96`, `app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:40-44`).
The entity-limited preset queue-id query is duplicated; a `TotemPreset` scope or method would keep the effective-scope rule in one place.
The RateLimiter registration is inserted between the `layouts` comment and the `Blade::anonymousComponentNamespace` call it describes, leaving the comment attached to unrelated code.
`priorities()` and `ticket()` reuse the `$queue` string route parameter for a `Queue|JsonResponse`, so the variable changes type mid-method and is harder to follow.

The helpers `pairedToken`, `bearer` and `setupTotem` are declared in a test file's global namespace; another test file defining the same names would fatal, so a shared helper file with unique names would be safer.

review.summary: The change implements the totem BFF end to end: schema, models and factories, the pairing command, HS256 JWT auth, the three scoped endpoints, throttling, CORS, docs, and a wide Pest suite. Behaviour and security look solid; the main reasons this is an approve-with-nits rather than as-is are the pairing domain write staying in the controller, an unrequested appearance-override feature, missing audit-log assertions, and checks on the dependency lock and doc accuracy.
